accepted.question_text: Find an explicit or recursive set-theoretic formula for a deterministic Cantor set on the real line that is generated by an iterated-function system with K >= 2 maps and that does not preserve bilateral symmetry.

evidence.quote: (OP1) Asymmetric constructions. Devise explicit or recursive set-theoretic formulas for Cantor sets generated by iterated-function systems (IFS) with K≥2 maps that do not preserve bilateral symmetry.

accepted.question_text: Find a descriptive formula for a deterministic Cantor set on the real line whose retained intervals have irrational end-points, allowing an iterated-function system with K >= 2 components.

evidence.quote: (OP2) Irrational end-points. Find descriptive formulas when the retained intervals have irrational end-points, again allowing K≥2 IFS components.

accepted.question_text: Given a sequence (alpha_n)_{n>=1} with 0 < alpha_n < 1 and 1 - sum_{n=1}^infinity 2^{n-1} alpha_n >= 0, give a recursive descriptive formula for the Cantor set obtained by the variable-gap middle-interval construction in which the open middle interval removed at stage n has length alpha_n.

evidence.quote: (OP3) Variable-gap deletions. Given a sequence (αn)n≥1 with 0 < αn < 1 satisfying 1 − P∞ n=1 2n−1 αn ≥ 0, provide a recursive descriptive formulae for the Cantor set obtained by removing at stage n the open middle interval of length αn.

accepted.question_text: For the variable-gap middle-interval Cantor-set construction determined by a sequence (alpha_n)_{n>=1} with 0 < alpha_n < 1 and 1 - sum_{n=1}^infinity 2^{n-1} alpha_n >= 0, determine how the answer to the recursive-description problem changes when bilateral symmetry is enforced versus when it is relaxed.

evidence.quote: (OP3) Variable-gap deletions. Given a sequence (αn)n≥1 with 0 < αn < 1 satisfying 1 − P∞ n=1 2n−1 αn ≥ 0, provide a recursive descriptive formulae for the Cantor set obtained by removing at stage n the open middle interval of length αn.
(OP4) Role of symmetry. Determine how the solution of problem (iii) varies when symmetry is either enforced or relaxed.

accepted.question_text: Establish conditions under which the Cantor-set families arising from the preceding four problems - asymmetric iterated-function-system constructions with K >= 2 maps, constructions with irrational retained end-points, variable-gap middle-interval deletions with parameters (alpha_n) satisfying 0 < alpha_n < 1 and 1 - sum_{n=1}^infinity 2^{n-1} alpha_n >= 0, and the symmetry-enforced or symmetry-relaxed versions of that variable-gap problem - have a non-empty mutual intersection.

evidence.quote: (OP1) Asymmetric constructions. Devise explicit or recursive set-theoretic formulas for Cantor sets generated by iterated-function systems (IFS) with K≥2 maps that do not preserve bilateral symmetry.
(OP2) Irrational end-points. Find descriptive formulas when the retained intervals have irrational end-points, again allowing K≥2 IFS components.

(OP3) Variable-gap deletions. Given a sequence (αn)n≥1 with 0 < αn < 1 satisfying 1 − P∞ n=1 2n−1 αn ≥ 0, provide a recursive descriptive formulae for the Cantor set obtained by removing at stage n the open middle interval of length αn.
(OP4) Role of symmetry. Determine how the solution of problem (iii) varies when symmetry is either enforced or relaxed.
(OP5) Common ground. Establish conditions under which the families arising in problems (i)-(iv) admit a non-empty mutual intersection.
